title: Compatibility and Sharp Joint-Intervention Bounds from Two Experiments on a Binary Collider
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental; projected paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4, with no bounded fix in scope; math review passed.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is nevertheless a closed-form specialization for one three-variable binary graph, one intervention menu, and one scalar risk already covered computationally by a published generic polynomial-program framework.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.

proof_attempt_summary: The D stage proved the closed-simplex compatibility frontier, the exact sharp interval, source-preserving finite-SCM attainment, rational endpoint certificates, a constant-operation procedure, and a conservative outer confidence interval; the D0.5 math panel passed. The result collapsed only on novelty: the fixed graph, intervention menu, and scalar query were rated incremental. Reaching the field floor would require a new, re-anchored dependence-budget sensitivity proposal rather than an in-scope repair.
tldr: For two complete experiments on the binary collider with two independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized tables \(A,B\), including structural zeros, are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\).  When compatible, the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the sharp closed interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One common deterministic outcome law with independent binary-valued source roots and at most eight private-root atoms attains every real interval point; rational inputs have exact rational endpoint certificates, yielding a constant-time fixed-graph procedure and an optional conservative outer sampling interval.
gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query numerically, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be consistent, but neither checked line supplies the graph-specific compatibility frontier, analytic endpoints, or a small common-SCM witness.
fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, resolves its source-preserving finite extension, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact certificate procedure for the same input handled generically by Autobounds.
